::: {#fig-flat-point-critical}

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

### R

```{r}
#| label: flat-point-critical-r
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Plot of w cubed minus 3w for w from -2.5 to 2.5. The blue curve rises to a
#|   local peak of 2 at w of -1, falls to a local trough of -2 at w of 1, then
#|   rises again. Vermilion circles mark the two flat points at w of -1 and w
#|   of 1.
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-width: 5
fpc_w_fk <- seq(-2.5, 2.5, length.out = 201)
fpc_curve_fk <- tibble::tibble(w = fpc_w_fk, value = fpc_w_fk^3 - 3 * fpc_w_fk)
fpc_flat_w_fk <- c(-1, 1)
fpc_flat_value_fk <- fpc_flat_w_fk^3 - 3 * fpc_flat_w_fk
fpc_flat_fk <- tibble::tibble(w = fpc_flat_w_fk, value = fpc_flat_value_fk)
fpc_aes_fk <- ggplot2::aes(w, value)
ggplot2::ggplot(fpc_curve_fk, fpc_aes_fk) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(colour = "#0072B2") +
  ggplot2::geom_point(data = fpc_flat_fk, colour = "#D55E00", size = 3) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "w", y = "f(w)")
```

### Python

```{python}
#| label: flat-point-critical-python
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Plot of w cubed minus 3w for w from -2.5 to 2.5. The blue curve rises to a
#|   local peak of 2 at w of -1, falls to a local trough of -2 at w of 1, then
#|   rises again. Vermilion circles mark the two flat points at w of -1 and w
#|   of 1.
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-width: 5
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

fpc_w_fk = np.linspace(-2.5, 2.5, 201)
fpc_flat_fk = np.array([-1, 1])
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 4), layout="constrained")
ax.plot(fpc_w_fk, fpc_w_fk**3 - 3 * fpc_w_fk, color="#0072B2")
ax.plot(fpc_flat_fk, fpc_flat_fk**3 - 3 * fpc_flat_fk, "o",
        color="#D55E00", markersize=8)
ax.set_xlabel("w")
ax.set_ylabel("f(w)")
plt.show()
```

:::

The [cubic](algebra.qmd#def-cubic-polynomial) $f(w) = w^3 - 3w$ of @exm-flat-point-critical.
Its [flat points](#def-flat-point),
where $f'(w) = 3w^2 - 3 = 0$,
are $w = -1$ and $w = 1$ (circles):
a local peak and a local trough.

:::
